title: Length of the Longest Increasing Path
summary: Given a 2D array of points and an index k, find the longest increasing path that includes the k-th point, where an increasing path requires each subsequent point to have both a greater x and y coordinate.
statement: Given a 2D array of points and an index k, find the longest increasing path that includes the k-th point, where an increasing path requires each subsequent point to have both a greater x and y coordinate.
constraints: coordinates contains up to 100,000 distinct 2D points and k is a valid index.
A path strictly increases both x and y and must contain coordinates[k].
Return its maximum possible number of points.
hints: Any valid target-containing path splits into points strictly southwest and strictly northeast of the target.
Compute a 2D strict LIS independently on each side, reversing signs for the northeast half.
Sort x ascending and y descending on x ties, then take a strict LIS of y with bisect_left.
Tie reversal prevents equal x values from chaining; the two independent paths join only through the target.
editorial: Tie reversal prevents equal x values from chaining; the two independent paths join only through the target.

tests.explanation: The path (0,0),(2,2),(5,3) contains the target and has length three.
Point (2,1) can precede the target (5,6), producing length two.
